stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They hypothesized that the type of exercise would affect memory.

**Participants.** The sample was 100 adults aged 60 to 75, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

**Results.** The group that walked briskly: mean locations recalled = 17. The group that did gentle stretching: mean locations recalled = 13. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?**

**Source A.** A survey of 1,200 teenagers found a correlation of r = +0.28 between hours of social media use per day and scores on a depression questionnaire. Teenagers who reported feeling lonely tended both to use social media more and to have higher depression scores.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 140 university students were randomly assigned either to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day for three weeks or to continue as usual. At the end, the limited group had a mean loneliness score of 38 and the usual-use group a mean of 45 (p = 0.03).

**Source C.** Researchers interviewed 40 teenagers about their experiences online. Many described feeling worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular; others described feeling supported by online friends who shared their interests.

questions.stem: Maya believes her grades depend entirely on how hard she works. Which belief does she hold?

options.why: The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.
Correct. An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true.

questions.explanation: An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Consent is obtained before the study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Replication is repeating a study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Replication is repeating a study.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Consent is obtained before the study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes massed practice?

options.text: The organizing of items into familiar, manageable units
options.why: That describes chunking.

options.text: The mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route
options.why: That describes the method of loci.

options.text: Study that is crammed into one long session
options.why: Correct. This is what massed practice means.

options.text: The organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones
options.why: That describes a hierarchy.

questions.explanation: Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.86, −0.44, +0.52, +0.05. Which coefficient shows the weakest relationship?

options.why: Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; +0.05 is closest to zero.
−0.44 is farther from zero.
+0.52 is farther from zero.
−0.86 is farther from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. +0.05 is closest to zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage?

options.why: Blindsight is the ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it.
Correct. Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.
Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.explanation: Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.

questions.stem: Mila constantly seeks out unfamiliar music, foreign films and trips to places she has never been. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Correct. Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.explanation: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted?

options.why: The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.
A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.
Correct. The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.
Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.

questions.explanation: The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption?

options.why: Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.
Correct. A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.
An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.
An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.

questions.explanation: A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.

questions.stem: A day after meeting twelve new people, Joy remembers only the names of the first two she met. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.
Correct. The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.explanation: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.

questions.stem: A two-year-old says 'Daddy go' and 'more cookie'. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Correct. Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.explanation: Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.

questions.stem: A therapist bluntly disputes his client's belief that 'everyone must like me or I am a failure.' Which therapy is this?

options.why: The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.
Correct. Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.

questions.explanation: Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.

questions.stem: Selye found that animals under prolonged stress passed through alarm, then resistance, then exhaustion. What is this three-phase pattern called?

options.why: The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.
The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.
Correct. The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.

questions.explanation: The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes nurture?

options.text: Research that compares adopted children with their biological and adoptive relatives
options.why: That describes an adoption study.

options.text: Research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity
options.why: That describes a twin study.

options.text: The influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes
options.why: Correct. This is what nurture means.

options.text: The discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans
options.why: That describes eugenics.

questions.explanation: Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food?

options.why: A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
Correct. The rooting reflex is a newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food.
A critical period is a limited time early in life when certain experiences must occur for normal development.
The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.

questions.explanation: The rooting reflex is a newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food.

questions.stem: Not wanting to upset the team's harmony, the members of a committee keep their doubts to themselves and approve a risky plan. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.
Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Correct. Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.

questions.explanation: Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person?

options.why: A longitudinal study is research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period.
Continuous development is the view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp.
A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.
Correct. Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.

questions.explanation: Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.

questions.stem: After being corrected, a toddler stops calling every four-legged animal a dog and learns a separate category for cows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Accommodation is the changing of an existing schema to fit new information.
Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.
A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.

questions.explanation: Accommodation is the changing of an existing schema to fit new information.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Replication is repeating a study.
Consent is obtained before the study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: When Ana becomes too hot, she sweats, and when she is cold, she shivers, keeping her body temperature near 37 degrees Celsius. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.
The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Correct. Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.

questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The warmth of parenting, as rated by observers
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: The level of financial stress in the family
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes avoidant attachment?

options.text: The attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return
options.why: That describes secure attachment.

options.text: The distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months
options.why: That describes separation anxiety.

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return
options.why: Correct. This is what avoidant attachment means.

options.text: The comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding
options.why: That describes contact comfort.

questions.explanation: Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose?

options.why: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
Correct. Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.

questions.explanation: Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations?

options.why: The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.
Correct. A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.
Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.

questions.explanation: A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes transduction?

options.text: The weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time
options.why: That describes the absolute threshold.

options.text: The way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste
options.why: That describes sensory interaction.

options.text: The smallest difference between two stimuli that a person can detect half of the time
options.why: That describes the just-noticeable difference.

options.text: The conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses
options.why: Correct. This is what transduction means.

questions.explanation: Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.

questions.stem: Leah is sure a fact is true but cannot remember whether she read it in a textbook or saw it in a film. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Correct. Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.

questions.explanation: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.stem: A brain scan shows strong activity in one structure when a person sees a threatening face. Which structure is it most likely to be?

options.why: The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
Correct. The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.explanation: The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.stem: An elderly woman's memory steadily worsens over several years until she no longer recognizes her family. Which condition does she most likely have?

options.why: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Correct. Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.stem: While studying, Vera notices that she does not really understand one section and decides to change her study method. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.
State-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same physical state as when the information was learned.
Context-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned.

questions.explanation: Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory?

options.why: The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
Correct. Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.explanation: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.stem: A psychologist shows a client a series of inkblots and asks what each might be. Which kind of test is this?

options.why: Correct. A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.
A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.

questions.explanation: A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.

questions.stem: A diagram labels every nerve that lies outside the brain and spinal cord. Which part of the nervous system does the diagram show?

options.why: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.
The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.
Correct. The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.

questions.explanation: The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes color constancy?

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes
options.why: That describes size constancy.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes
options.why: That describes shape constancy.

options.text: The perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession
options.why: That describes apparent movement.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting
options.why: Correct. This is what color constancy means.

questions.explanation: Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 13, 9, 4, 17, 7, 11, 9. What is the median of the scores?

options.why: Correct. Put the scores in order and take the middle one, the fourth of seven.
That is the mean.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 4, 7, 9, 9, 11, 13, 17. Put the scores in order and take the middle one, the fourth of seven. The one very high score pulls the mean (10) above the median (9), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: The group that first signed the petition agreed more often. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: Whether a small request came first and compliance with a large request are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: Whether a small request came first caused the difference in compliance with a large request
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: The word 'chat' has three basic sounds: ch, a and t. Each of these sounds is which of the following?

options.why: Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.
Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.
A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.
Correct. A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.

questions.explanation: A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes texture gradient?

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away
options.why: Correct. This is what texture gradient means.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer
options.why: That describes interposition.

options.text: The binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object
options.why: That describes convergence.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which hazy objects are seen as farther away than sharp ones
options.why: That describes relative clarity.

questions.explanation: Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes generalized anxiety disorder?

options.text: The disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations
options.why: That describes social anxiety disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months
options.why: Correct. This is what generalized anxiety disorder means.

options.text: The disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult
options.why: That describes agoraphobia.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation
options.why: That describes a specific phobia.

questions.explanation: Generalized anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it?

options.why: Correct. Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: The group with mismatched colors named fewer flavors correctly. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The color of the drinks caused the difference in flavor identification
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The color of the drinks and flavor identification are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships?

options.why: Correct. Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.
Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.
The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.
Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.

questions.explanation: Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.

questions.stem: Nina wants the chocolate cake because it tastes wonderful but does not want it because it is unhealthy. Which kind of conflict is this?

options.why: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
Correct. An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.

questions.explanation: An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.

questions.stem: For a week, a patient sleeps two hours a night, speaks rapidly, starts ten projects and feels invincible. Which state is this?

options.why: Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Correct. Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.
Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.explanation: Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.stem: Ice cream sales and drownings rise together, but both are caused by hot weather. Which problem does this illustrate?

options.why: A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
Correct. The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.

questions.explanation: The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the tend-and-befriend response?

options.text: The response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support
options.why: Correct. This is what the tend-and-befriend response means.

options.text: The response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape
options.why: That describes the fight-or-flight response.

options.text: The field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness
options.why: That describes health psychology.

options.text: An event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging
options.why: That describes a stressor.

questions.explanation: The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.

questions.stem: Which receptor cells let a person see the colors and fine details of a painting in daylight?

options.why: The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.
The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.
Correct. Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.
The lens is the transparent structure that changes shape to focus light on the retina.

questions.explanation: Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

options.text: The behavior of an adult model
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: A researcher who expects a drug to work smiles more at the patients who receive it and rates their improvement more generously. Which bias is this?

options.why: Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.
Correct. Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.

questions.explanation: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Experiments also use numerical data.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the biopsychosocial model?

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: Correct. This is what the biopsychosocial model means.

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: That describes comorbidity.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: That describes the diathesis-stress model.

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: That describes an eclectic approach.

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes projection?

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: That describes rationalization.

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: That describes displacement.

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: Correct. This is what projection means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: That describes denial.

questions.explanation: Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.

questions.stem: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The number of other people present and the reporting of an emergency are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The number of other people present caused the difference in the reporting of an emergency
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Several times a week, Ron eats far more than he intends, feels ashamed afterward, but does not vomit or fast. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Correct. Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.
Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.

questions.explanation: Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.

questions.stem: Fans rate players on their own team as more skilled and more honest than equally good players on other teams. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.
Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.

questions.explanation: In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.stem: A theory says that neurons alternate firing, like soldiers taking turns shooting, to keep up with sounds faster than one neuron can fire. Which theory is this?

options.why: Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.
Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.
Correct. Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.

questions.explanation: Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.

questions.stem: Although the film is terrible, Mo stays to the end because he already paid for the ticket. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.
The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.
Correct. The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.
Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.

questions.explanation: The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.

questions.stem: A five-year-old realizes that his sister will look for her doll where she left it, even though he knows it has been moved. What has he developed?

options.why: Conservation is the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes.
Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.
Correct. Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.
Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.

questions.explanation: Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.

questions.stem: To treat alcohol misuse, a client is given a drug that causes nausea whenever he drinks. Which treatment is this?

options.why: Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.
Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.
Correct. Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.

questions.explanation: Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.48. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: After watching her older brother tie his shoes, four-year-old Lily ties her own in the same way. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
Correct. Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.
Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.

questions.explanation: Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes cultural humility?

options.text: The movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care
options.why: That describes deinstitutionalization.

options.text: A therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view
options.why: Correct. This is what cultural humility means.

options.text: The choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values
options.why: That describes evidence-based practice.

options.text: The bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client
options.why: That describes the therapeutic alliance.

questions.explanation: Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: In the middle of laughing at a joke, Viktor suddenly falls asleep. Which sleep disorder does he most likely have?

options.why: Correct. Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.
Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.
Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.explanation: Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being?

options.why: The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
Correct. An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.

questions.explanation: An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 80 university students. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: For most people, speech is controlled mainly by the left hemisphere, while recognizing faces relies more on the right. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Correct. Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.

questions.explanation: Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.

questions.stem: A previously healthy student suddenly develops hallucinations after a period of intense stress and later recovers well. Which pattern of onset is this?

options.why: The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
Correct. An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.

questions.explanation: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes random sampling?

options.text: The extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample
options.why: That describes generalizability.

options.text: A flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population
options.why: That describes sampling bias.

options.text: A sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from
options.why: That describes a representative sample.

options.text: The selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen
options.why: Correct. This is what random sampling means.

questions.explanation: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

questions.stem: Around age 51, Mrs. Ortiz's menstrual cycles stop permanently. Which term describes this change?

options.why: Correct. Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.
Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.
Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.

questions.explanation: Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes informed assent?

options.text: The requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible
options.why: That describes protection from harm.

options.text: The misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing
options.why: That describes deception.

options.text: The agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent
options.why: Correct. This is what informed assent means.

options.text: A person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher
options.why: That describes a confederate.

questions.explanation: Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.

questions.stem: Kim remembers exactly where she sat and what she ate at her tenth birthday party. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Correct. Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.explanation: Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.stem: To remember the term 'hippocampus', Sol links it to a hippo on a campus who never forgets his classes. Which technique is he using?

options.why: Correct. Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.explanation: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of memory

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of memory.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Memory was defined as the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The walking group recalled more locations. On average, the value was 17 for the group that walked briskly and 13 for the group that did gentle stretching, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 100 adults aged 60 to 75 from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The walking group recalled more locations. (17 compared with 13).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the type of exercise affects memory. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the type of exercise. The finding illustrates neuroplasticity: experience such as exercise can change the brain, including the hippocampus, which forms new memories.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Heavy social media use can harm teenagers' well-being, especially when it leads them to compare themselves with others.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who limited social media to 30 minutes a day had lower loneliness scores (38) than students who continued as usual (45).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because the study was an experiment with random assignment, so reducing social media use can be said to have caused the lower loneliness. Less time online leaves more time for face-to-face contact, which supports well-being.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source C, many teenagers said they felt worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through upward social comparison and relative deprivation: comparing oneself with people who seem better off lowers self-esteem and satisfaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
